title: Sum of Two Integers
description: Given two integers `a` and `b`, return their sum **without using the `+` or `-` operators**. Negative numbers must be handled correctly.
hints: Add two bits by hand: which bitwise operation gives the digit, and which gives the carry?
a ^ b is the sum ignoring carries; (a & b) << 1 is the carries. Add those two the same way until no carry is left.
Python integers never overflow, so negative numbers would loop forever. Mask to 32 bits with 0xFFFFFFFF each step, and at the end convert values above 0x7FFFFFFF back to negative.

solution.explanation: XOR adds two numbers ignoring carries, and (a & b) << 1 produces the carries; repeat with the new pair until the carry is zero. Python ints are unbounded, so a negative carry would keep shifting forever. The 32-bit mask trick fixes this: AND both values with 0xFFFFFFFF on every step to emulate 32-bit two's complement, and at the end, if the result exceeds 0x7FFFFFFF, convert it back to negative with ~(a ^ mask). The loop runs at most 32 times, so time and space are O(1).
